reviewer: builder (the agent session that wrote the generator)
findings: The plan reads as a half-ellipse crescent of eighteen houses, as the street view and the oblique show.
Three storeys: a plain ground storey, then two storeys behind a giant Ionic order with one sash to a window bay on each.
Each corner has a corner column and a partner 0.95 m along each face with blind wall between; each end has nine columns and six window bays.
Each end roof is a true hip: one slate face over every point, with the hips running corner to corner and two dormers on the end slope.
Every chimney stack stands through the roof; none has air under its base.
Plain walling shows no hairlines: each bay of wall is a grid of faces sharing every corner with its neighbours.
Entablature, modillion cornice and balustrade run unbroken round all four sides; capitals and pedestals at the corners are square to the faces.
Every sash sits in a reveal with a frame, six panes over six and glass, with floors and walls behind; every door has panels, a fanlight and a threshold.
The door layout mirrors about the middle: the middle bay of each house, with the two end houses entered from their ends.
The convex side and both ends are complete elevations. Nothing floats and nothing sits below grade.

response_to_independent_review_of_v002.P1-04 rear_side cropped: Fixed. Every whole view is checked by projecting the outline through its camera; none comes nearer the frame than 6 percent.

response_to_independent_review_of_v002.P2-02 roof-plan reference: Unchanged and declared: it shows a different building.

response_to_independent_review_of_v002.P2-10 panel joints: Fixed. Walls are grids of faces with shared corners.

open_notes: The roof plan reference shows a different, shorter building; it informs roof character only.
Sunken areas, their steps and the bridges to the doors are left out; railings stand at grade.
Garden doors on the convex side are an invention.
Bays on the convex side widen toward the ends, from 2.7 m to 4.0 m.
Each corner room at the two ends has windows in two walls, so a diagonal line of sight passes through glass alone there.
Over about a square metre beside each outer corner the slate lies up to 0.26 m from the ideal roof surface, where flat faces turn a curved plan.
Thin railing bars and glazing bars break up in distant views; a renderer sampling effect.
